title: Mainstreet Brass plays a free Christmas concert at St. John's Lutheran on Dec. 6
summary: The brass quintet, which also plays for the Bethlehem Bach Festival, brings carols and holiday TV favorites to the church's concert series on Sunday, Dec. 6 at 4 p.m. Admission is free, with a suggested $10 freewill offering.
loc: St. John's Lutheran Church, 355 St. John's Circle, Phoenixville

title: Pottstown Dance Theatre brings The Nutcracker back Dec. 12 and 13
summary: The company's Repertory Ensemble, made up of its students and teachers and directed by Michelle Jones Wurtz, performs at Pottstown Area High School on Saturday, Dec. 12 at 7 p.m. and Sunday, Dec. 13 at 2 p.m. The Greater Pottstown Foundation is a partial sponsor.
loc: Pottstown Area High School, 750 N. Washington St., Pottstown

title: Valley Forge Tourism's hunger drive is 85% of the way to its 250,000-pound goal
summary: The 12th annual Freedom from Hunger campaign has raised the cash equivalent of just under 213,000 pounds of food for the MontCo Anti-Hunger Network's 70-plus pantries and meal programs. The online drive runs through the holidays, with results expected in late December or early January.

title: Holiday pop-up bar and gift shop opens weekends on Gay Street
summary: The Holiday Collective, run by U Pretty Things Boutique, pairs gift shopping with a cash bar and a mixologist at 8 Gay St. It is open Fridays and Saturdays from 11 a.m. to 8 p.m., Nov. 28 through Dec. 20.

title: Sanatoga Road closes Nov. 30 for three weeks of Route 422 bridge demolition
summary: PennDOT will shut Sanatoga Road between High Street and Linfield Road around the clock from Nov. 30 through Dec. 21 while crews take down bridges on the $83.6 million Route 422 rebuild. Westbound 422 also loses its left lane overnight Dec. 1 to 3 between the Sanatoga and Hanover Street interchanges.
loc: Route 422 at Sanatoga Road, Lower Pottsgrove

title: Colonial Theatre makes Drew Boardman its executive director
summary: Boardman, who has led the theater on an interim basis since July, gets the job permanently. He was previously the Colonial's events director and artistic director.
loc: The Colonial Theatre, Bridge Street, Phoenixville

title: Spring City gets an indoor golf lounge and a bargain bin store
summary: The Turn, a virtual golf center with simulator bays, opens Friday, Nov. 27 at 20 Bonnie Brae Road. Bin to Win, selling overstock, returned and clearance goods from big retailers, has opened at 65 E. Bridge St.
loc: Bonnie Brae Road and E. Bridge Street, Spring City

title: Nashville-style honky-tonk headed for the old Iron Hill Brewery on Bridge Street
summary: Phoenixville Honky Tonk will fill 130 Bridge Street, empty since Iron Hill closed there in fall 2024, with live country music, line dancing, Southern-style food and drinks. The owners have not announced an opening date yet.

title: Facet Life Sciences CEO Ken VanLuvanee dies
summary: The co-founder of the Phoenixville-based regulatory consulting firm, a borough resident since 2003, died Nov. 13. His wife and co-founder, Lisa Jenkins VanLuvanee, now leads the roughly 40-person company, with Tom Meyer as president.

title: La Patrona closes its Bridge Street restaurant Nov. 22
summary: The Mexican restaurant and tequila bar ends five years downtown with a final service on Sunday, Nov. 22. The owners say they are looking for a new location and hope to reopen, possibly in a different format.
